about: Ship Desk: TCGplayer shipping CSV -> address labels, packing slips, envelopes, shipping plan + stamps, mark-shipped import file (local, offline browser app)

runs.title: First build of Ship Desk + landscape thermal label
runs.summary: A 4-station nodeterm team built a local copy of what tcgspeedshipper.com does from one contract; QA proved it end to end (113 tests), then a landscape 6x4 thermal label was added (117 tests).

stages.name: Plan
stages.note: research, contract, briefs, test harness, vendored libraries

sessions.did: Read the site and sample CSV, wrote CONTRACT.md + 4 briefs, serve.py, headless-Edge test harness, vendored jsPDF/pdf.js/qrcode
CSV reader, shipping plan + stamps, tracking match, TCGplayer import + Pirate Ship files, paste parser, sample CSV; 39 tests
8 label formats, packing slips, design options, TCGplayer slip-PDF reader; 50 tests
4-step page, return-address profiles, offline service worker, Start Ship Desk.bat; 13 tests

stages.name: QA
stages.note: armed after-success on all three builders

sessions.did: 9 end-to-end tests (113 total), 16 screenshots checked, README + test report, 3 small fixes
Re-ran all tests, looked at screenshots, added landscape thermal 6x4 label (117 tests)

lessons: A test harness proven before launch (headless Edge, results POSTed back) let every station test on a PC without Node.
File ownership + a Requests section in each brief kept parallel stations out of each other's files.
Check each vendored download separately: one failed silently in an && chain.

runs.title: History tab + Saved folder
runs.summary: The orchestrator session added a History page of every order labelled or shipped, and made every generated file save into Ship Desk's own Saved folder instead of Downloads (130 tests).

sessions.did: history.js + History page; serve.py /api/save + /api/open-folder, Saved/ gitignored; 13 new tests

lessons: Files a local app writes for the user that hold customer data must be gitignored before the first write when the repo is public.
A localhost endpoint that writes files must check Host, Origin and a custom header, or any website the user visits can write there.

runs.title: Phone photos, label scanning, sideways label fix
runs.summary: The orchestrator session added an iPhone page for order photos (through Tailscale, with an offline queue), fixed the cut-off sideways label, and added order QR codes plus mailer tracking-barcode scanning that feeds History (144 tests).

sessions.did: phone.html/js + offline IndexedDB queue, serve.py phone API + Tailscale switch + pairing code, History photos; sideways label as upright page; order QR on prints, zxing scanner, tracking links into History; 14 new tests

lessons: Thermal printers don't rotate a wide PDF page onto a narrow roll; they cut it off. Draw a landscape label turned on an upright page.
An iPhone that can't reach the PC on a double-NAT LAN can use `tailscale serve` (tailnet only) with the server still on 127.0.0.1; treat proxied requests as a separate, restricted client.
Headless --virtual-time-budget screenshots don't wait for IndexedDB; use real-time DevTools capture.
A canvas captureStream() makes a fake camera for testing getUserMedia scanners in headless Edge.

runs.title: Mailer entries, camera screen, post office = shipped, photo turning
runs.summary: The orchestrator session turned unknown mailer scans into History entries, made the scanner a multi-photo camera that turns sideways shots upright, marked orders shipped from post office photos, and added photo turn buttons on the PC (148 tests).

sessions.did: mailer:<tracking> entries + Add order # in History with photo re-key; camera screen with shutter, type switch and tilt-based turning; post office photo -> shipped note; PC photo turn buttons; Windows file-replace retry; 4 new tests

events.text: A failed patch script emptied app/js/phone.js; rebuilt from git and re-applied

lessons: Write a file only after its new content is fully encoded: open(..., 'w') empties it before a failing write.
On Windows, os.replace onto a JSON file that another thread is reading raises PermissionError: retry briefly.
Photos shot straight down at a desk lose their orientation; a web camera can use devicemotion gravity and keep the last turn while flat.

runs.title: File names that say what is inside, camera asked for once
runs.summary: The orchestrator session named saved files by time and buyers and kept the phone camera ready between uses so the iPhone stops re-asking (148 tests).

sessions.did: fileName() for labels/slips/import/Pirate Ship/history, wider NAME_OK; camera stream kept 5 min after Done and reused; tests updated

lessons: An iPhone home-screen web app re-asks for the camera on each getUserMedia call: keep and reuse the stream for a while.

runs.title: Tracking barcodes read much better
runs.summary: The orchestrator session benchmarked barcode reading on 96 phone-like mailer pictures, found zxing-js failing beside darker mailers, and switched the phone to zxing-wasm (15 -> 50 of 96) with a JS fallback (150 tests).

sessions.did: barcode benchmark; JS strip reader with local thresholds; zxing-wasm 3.1.6 vendored as main reader; serve.py wasm type + phone files; 2 new tests

lessons: zxing-js 1D reading uses a whole-row threshold: a dark surface beside a white label makes it fail; zxing-wasm (zxing-cpp) read 3x more phone-like barcode pictures.
Measure barcode readers on generated camera-like pictures (blur, tilt, grain, background) before tuning.

runs.title: On/off switch, background, start with Windows
runs.summary: The orchestrator session added an on/off switch to the page (shutdown + shipdesk://start), made Ship Desk run windowless in the background, fixed two copies sharing the port, and added Start with Windows (152 tests).

sessions.did: header on/off switch, /api/ping + /api/shutdown, shipdesk:// launcher; pythonw background start, log, Stop bat; SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE; Start with Windows (HKCU Run); 2 new tests; live checks

events.text: Live test found two Ship Desks on one port (old window re-ran the edited .bat); fixed with an exclusive port

lessons: On Windows, Python http.server sets SO_REUSEADDR, so a second server can bind the same port: use SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE.
cmd reads a running .bat from disk as it goes: editing it while an old window runs it can run the new lines.

runs.title: History copy, sent to TCGplayer, proof packs
runs.summary: The orchestrator session suggested ten improvements and built the top three: a History copy on the PC with a safe restore, import files that only carry what is new, and a proof-pack PDF per order (155 tests).

sessions.did: /api/history-copy + linked-browser offer/restore; sent-to-TCGplayer marks + skipSent import; proofPack PDF; phone status fix; 3 new tests

lessons: A browser-only store needs a copy on disk, but a browser that lost its data must not overwrite the copy: link the browser first and offer a restore otherwise.

runs.title: First real TCGplayer upload
runs.summary: The user uploaded a real import file; TCGplayer refused the empty carrier on an untracked row, the session set Carrier USPS and the re-upload imported cleanly (155 tests).

sessions.did: read the error screenshot, Carrier USPS for Shipped rows, tests + docs; confirmed by the user re-upload

events.text: Real TCGplayer upload: 1 row successfully imported, 0 errors

lessons: When a site's help pages can't be read, let the real upload's error screen decide the format.

runs.title: Security audit and fixes
runs.summary: A security-auditor subagent audited the week's new parts (0 critical/high/medium, 3 low); the orchestrator fixed all three lows the same day (158 tests).

sessions.did: full audit, offline proofs p1-p5, report 2026-10-25-Shipping.md: __proto__ key, CSV formulas, missing headers; 4 info
valid_order_key + own() lookups, spreadsheetSafe CSV, CSP and headers, README wording; 3 new tests; restart

lessons: Objects keyed by data from outside (order keys) need own-property lookups and a key whitelist on the server: __proto__ reached every record.
After adding a Content-Security-Policy, test that features with fallbacks (WebAssembly reader) still use the main path, not just that tests pass.

runs.title: Orders survive a reload; tracking from Pirate Ship's export
runs.summary: One session kept the loaded batch across reloads (Clear button, 14 days) and added reading Pirate Ship's Shipments export (.xlsx) to put tracking numbers on orders by buyer name; 164 tests.

sessions.did: Batch kept in the browser + Clear these orders; pirate.js (.xlsx reader, name matching), applyShipments, sample export, tests 158 -> 164

lessons: Pirate Ship has two exports: Transactions (money, no tracking) and Shipments (tracking, but no order # or ZIP), so matching is by name and date.

runs.title: Hourly backup of Saved to OneDrive
runs.summary: The same session added an hourly OneDrive backup of the Saved folder (user's choice of place), restarted Ship Desk at the user's OK and ran the first backup (218 files); 165 tests.

sessions.did: serve.py backup (copy new/changed, skip pairing code + log, hourly thread), History page switch, test folder fake, first real backup

lessons: tailscale serve listens on the same port number on the tailnet addresses: check 127.0.0.1 when waiting for the local server to stop.

runs.title: Backup moved to Dropbox
runs.summary: The same session made the backup place a choice (Dropbox or OneDrive), moved it to Dropbox at the user's request, checked the copy and deleted the OneDrive one; 165 tests.

sessions.did: Dropbox/OneDrive place setting + menu, one-step switch, restart, first Dropbox backup (218 files), old OneDrive copy deleted

lessons: A test wait helper that treats any truthy value as done returns at once for an async check (a promise): poll with await.

runs.title: Phone To do list
runs.summary: The same session added a To do view on the phone: orders grouped by the photo they need next, with a one-tap camera button and one photo for the post office pile; 166 tests.

sessions.did: phone.js To do view (nextPhoto, todoGroups, Picked group), camera buttons, styles, test, phone screenshots

lessons: A new default view must keep showing what the old one always showed (picked orders): two older tests caught it.

runs.title: One post office photo per order; step through the pile
runs.summary: At the user's request each post office photo now goes only to the order just scanned, and the To do list steps through the post office pile one order at a time; 167 tests.

sessions.did: shoot() targets scan.fresh / lastPost for post office photos, step-through mode (nextStep, ▶ chip, skip), tests

lessons: Headless Edge: don't await a camera start in tests, and keep repainting a canvas used as a fake camera (captureStream only sends frames on change).

runs.title: Real packing slip; item reader fixed
runs.summary: The user's first real TCGplayer slip printed right but showed the item reader took the game as the card name and lost the wrapped line; fixed and checked on the real slip; 169 tests.

sessions.did: Read the real slip layout (item lines only), describeItem + wrapped-line joining in slips.js, real-slip dry run, 2 tests

lessons: Headless Edge --dump-dom returns before async work (a pdf.js worker) finishes: have the page POST its result to a small local server instead.

runs.title: Windows installer 1.0.0 and MIT licence
runs.summary: The same session built a per-user Windows installer with its own Python (Inno Setup), tested install/run/uninstall without touching the user's copy (after one accidental stop, fixed), added the MIT licence and prepared the GitHub release.

sessions.did: build_installer.py, ShipDesk.iss, serve.py data_root/--stop, notices, guide converter, install tests, LICENSE, release notes

events.text: Install test's --stop turned off the user's Ship Desk for about a minute; restarted and fixed
gh release create blocked by auto mode; left for the user to run

lessons: A stop command for 'this copy only' must refuse when the running copy can't say where it runs from.
Silent Inno installs take the default-ticked tasks: name them off (/MERGETASKS) when testing on a real PC.

sessions.did: serve.py tailscale install/login/enable link + update check, app.js phone steps 1-4, welcome checklist, update banner, test stand-ins, installer task, upgrade test

lessons: A first-run checklist must redraw on every setting that can tick it (its test caught the return address).

events.text: First automatic build stopped on a test timeout (page start > 8 s under load); waits raised to 20 s, second build passed

lessons: A Ship Desk import file must not depend on which file is loaded: orders are shipped days after their labels.

stages.name: Audit
stages.note: subagent of af0659e3, read-only on the project

sessions.did: Full audit of the 1.1 additions: 129/129 attack requests refused; uninstall DelTree, OneDrive default folder, loose Tailscale signer check (low), Python 3.14.7, ts.net name in CT logs (info)

orderlist.js + applyOrderList, notsent filter, all audit fixes (installer marker/own folder, signer fields, Python 3.14.10), tracked-envelope plan setting, imb.js (USPS IMb encode/decode/find), barcode on labels; 188 tests; ported fixCode128 from the old branch, removed its worktree; installer 1.1.3 built, tested, published

events.text: Context paused 2026-10-26 to 2026-10-29; TCGplayer announced tracked envelopes 2026-10-27

lessons: Bash heredocs turned \n in JS test strings into real line breaks again: patch scripts go through the Write tool.
A barcode check that needed half a bar's height to overlap failed on label renders by one pixel: 0.3 is safe.
An old branch can be behind main by dozens of commits: compare its base before merging, port the one useful piece with a test that fails without it, and record the branch merged with -s ours.

runs.title: Envelope labels from TCGplayer's tracked slips
runs.summary: With the first real tracked slip: the USPS barcode is read from the slip's text with its checked address, the new slip's item rows are read again, and three envelope-label formats (2 per 4x6, 6x4 landscape, 8 per letter) print return address + barcode + address for plain envelopes; checked on the user's printed label from a phone photo.

sessions.did: imbFromRows (barcode as text + address), new item-row layout, drawCutLabel + thermalCut/thermalEnvelope/envelopeCut, one-click button, reload notice, safety research (USPS ok, TCGplayer wants window envelopes); 206 tests

lessons: The user's first two PDFs came from the cached old app: a service-worker app needs an 'updated, reload' notice, not 'reload twice'.
A real sample beats guesses: TCGplayer's barcode was text in a font, so reading the text is exact where a picture search was the plan.
The project's repo is public: log real orders' numbers and ZIPs nowhere, only what was checked.

runs.title: 1.1.4 published; a no-install zip for PCs that warn about the installer
runs.summary: Published 1.1.4, then, for the user's Windows/antivirus warning, added a zip of Ship Desk that needs no installing (only Python's signed programs and two .bat files), tested unzipped and added to the 1.1.4 release.

sessions.did: gh release v1.1.4; looked for Defender detections (none, McAfee is this PC's antivirus); signing options researched; build_installer.py makes ShipDesk-<v>-portable.zip (+ --zip-only), tools/test_portable.py 18 checks; zip uploaded

lessons: Ask what the warning actually said before fixing it: SmartScreen's 'unrecognized app' box and a Defender virus alarm need different fixes.
The user cut the question short with a better idea (a zip): a zip of signed programs sidesteps the unsigned installer without paying for a certificate.

lessons: Try a link before shipping it: USPS's tracking page doesn't find IMb numbers; the user's example link (TCGplayer's tracking page) showed the right number form (20 digits + ZIP).
Check what already works before building it: dropping the slip PDF on the page already worked; the page just never said so.
